title: The shoemaker and the elves.
lines: Once upon a time there was a shoemaker.
He lived with his wife in a little house in a little street.
He made the most beautiful shoes in the whole village.
But he had grown old and he didn't work so fast anymore.
People preferred to buy their shoes in the big shop in town.
That's why the shoemaker was very poor.
One evening he had only one small piece of leather left.
Enough for one pair of shoes.
Tomorrow I'll make my last pair of shoes, he sighed.
He cut the leather into the right shape.
He laid the pieces ready on his workbench, together with the needle and thread.
Then he went to sleep.
The next morning the shoemaker came into his workshop.
He rubbed his eyes.
What did he see?
On the table stood a pair of shoes.
All finished!
The stitches were tiny and very neat.
The shoes were shiny.
They were the most beautiful shoes he had ever seen.
Wife!
he called.
Come and look!
Who did this?
His wife didn't know either.
That day a rich gentleman came into the shop.
He saw the shoes and tried them on.
They fit perfectly!
He paid a lot of money for them.
With that money the shoemaker bought leather for two pairs of shoes.
That evening he cut everything out again and went to sleep.
And the next morning?
Two pairs of shoes, all finished!
It went like that every night.
A pair of boots.
A pair of sandals.
A pair of dancing shoes for a princess.
The shoemaker sold them all.
He wasn't poor anymore.
But who was helping him?
One evening, just before Christmas, his wife said: You know what?
Let's hide tonight.
Then we'll see who is helping us.
They hid behind a curtain.
They left a candle burning.
At midnight they heard a soft little sound.
Tap, tap, tap.
Two tiny elves came in through the window.
They had pointy little ears.
But they wore no clothes, just a few old rags.
They were barefoot.
The elves jumped onto the table.
They took the needle and thread.
They sewed and they tapped with a tiny hammer.
Tap, tap, tap.
They worked very fast.
They sang a song while they worked.
Before the sun came up, all the shoes were finished.
And whoosh, off they went, through the window.
The shoemaker and his wife looked at each other.
Those sweet elves, said the wife.
They help us every night.
But they are so cold themselves.
They don't even have clothes.
Let's give them something back.
The wife sewed two little shirts, two pairs of trousers and two jackets.
She knitted two pairs of socks.
And the shoemaker made two pairs of tiny shoes, the most beautiful he ever made.
On Christmas Eve they laid everything on the table, instead of the leather.
At midnight the elves came again.
They saw the little clothes.
They looked surprised.
Then they put everything on.
The shirts, the trousers, the jackets, the socks and the shoes.
Everything fit perfectly.
The elves danced across the table with joy.
They skipped and they laughed.
And they sang: Now we are two fine little gentlemen, why should we be shoemakers anymore?
And they danced out of the window, into the night.
The elves never came back.
But that was all right.
The shoemaker had learned how they made such lovely, tiny stitches.
His shoes were now the most famous in the land.
And every Christmas Eve the shoemaker and his wife put a little present on the windowsill.
For the elves.
You never know.
The end.
